sections.title: Basic Concept of Radar and Web Chart
sections.content: In a Radar or Web chart, data is represented in a circular form. Each axis represents a category. Step 1: Identify all axes and their values. Step 2: Understand the scale (like 10, 20, 30). Step 3: Compare different categories.

sections.title: Finding Average
sections.content: Step 1: Add all values. Step 2: Divide the total by the number of items. Step 3: Get the answer. Example: Marks of 5 subjects = 20, 30, 40, 50, 60 → average = (200/5) = 40.

sections.title: Finding Ratio
sections.content: Step 1: Take values of two categories. Step 2: Divide both values. Step 3: Convert into simplest form. Example: A = 40, B = 20 → ratio = 40:20 = 2:1.

sections.title: Finding Percentage
sections.content: Step 1: Identify part and total. Step 2: Apply (part/total) × 100. Step 3: Get the percentage. Example: 40 out of 80 → (40/80) × 100 = 50%.

sections.title: Making Comparison
sections.content: Step 1: Look at values of two or more categories. Step 2: Find difference or ratio. Step 3: Identify highest and lowest values.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Reading the scale incorrectly. 2. Estimating values wrongly. 3. Adding totals incorrectly in average. 4. Not simplifying ratios.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: In Radar/Web DI, questions mainly involve average, ratio, and percentage. By reading the correct scale and doing basic calculations, answers can be found quickly.

tricks.title: Quick Average Trick
tricks.explanation: If numbers are equally spaced, the middle value is the average.

tricks.title: Ratio Simplify Shortcut
tricks.explanation: Divide both numbers by their common factor.

tricks.title: Percentage Fast Method
tricks.explanation: Convert part/total into a fraction for quick calculation.

tricks.title: Difference Check Trick
tricks.explanation: Quickly find the difference between two values.

tricks.title: Scale Reading Shortcut
tricks.explanation: Understand the chart scale first, then read values.

tricks.title: Identify Highest-Lowest
tricks.explanation: Quickly spot the largest and smallest values.

tricks.title: Quick Comparison Trick
tricks.example: 45 is greater than 30, so it is larger.
